name: Tarocchi Siciliano
description: Tarocchi Siciliano (Sicilian Tarot) is a traditional card game played with a unique 63-card deck. It features ranks and suits distinct from other Tarot decks (Portuguese-style pips). The game is a point-trick game, often played by 4 players. Features the 'Fugitive' (Fool) and 'Miseria' (low trump).

history.origins: Developed in Sicily; retained Portuguese-style suits after they disappeared elsewhere.
timeline: 18th century: Deck shortened from 78 to 63 cards; Portuguese-style suits retained in Sicily.
history.cultural: Played in towns like Mineo, Tortorici, Barcellona Pozzo di Gotto.

setup.deck: 63 cards: 4 suits (King, Queen, Knight, Page, 10-5, Coins has 4) + 21 Trumps + Fugitive.

rules.objective: Take more than half the card points (55 or more of 109) in tricks; win last trick (Vanto) and other bonuses (Pigliata, 4 Re, Arie) for jochi. Soloist plays alone against the others; in 4-player, caller may name a trump to get a secret partner.
rules.gameplay: Must follow suit. Must trump if void. Fugitive (Fool) is excuse. Trumps 20-1 (highest to lowest), plus Miseria (lowest).

strategy.basic: Conserve high trumps. Use Fugitive to save a King.

variations.name: Mineo three-player
variations.description: 20 cards each, 3-card monte; soloist takes monte and discards three. Solo or abandon with mischio/pago/prendo. Vado solo possible after 5 or 20 cards.

variations.name: Mineo four-player
variations.description: 15 cards each, 3-card monte. Bidding: pass, chiamo (call a trump for secret partner), or vado solo. Caller names highest trump not held; holder is partner.

scoring.description: 109 card points total. Batches of three count minus 2; last trick +5. Trump 20, 1, Fool 10 each; trumps 16-19 and Kings 5; Queens 4, Horses 3, Maids 2; others 1.
scoring.winCondition: Take more than half (55+) card points; win last trick and bonuses for jochi.
